source: a hand-made reading of the API, not generated; see contract/README.md

authSchemes.note: the published OpenAPI description lists only basicAuth; the application-key scheme is recorded from observed behaviour and no automated gate can cover it

dispatch.warning: any colon ANYWHERE after the 'Application ' prefix routes here; never append to the key

verificationErrorCodesNote: destination_not_supported_for_channel is the outcome of a failed verification (an unsupported destination is a 201 with status failed) and stays in the envelope list for compatibility. stale_dispatch is no longer sent - those verifications are reported as dispatch_failed - and is kept, deprecated, only so existing matches still compile

errorDetails.delivery_method_inclusion: delivery method is not included in the list
errorDetails.sms_domain_not_configured: application has no SMS domain configured
errorDetails.destination_not_supported_for_channel: destination not supported for provided delivery method
errorDetails.already_verified: verification is already verified; provided value is invalid
errorDetails.not_ready_to_report: verification is not ready to be reported
errorDetails.parameter_missing: request body must contain a valid data object
errorDetails.destination_in_cooldown: verification for this destination was requested too recently
errorDetails.rate_limit_per_ip: too many requests from this IP address; contact support to raise the limit
errorDetails.rate_limit_failed_auth: too many failed authentication attempts from this IP address; try again later
errorDetails.rate_limit_per_account: too many requests for this account; contact support to raise the limit
errorDetails.rate_limit_public_per_account: too many public requests for this account; contact support to raise the limit
errorDetails.volume_limit_reached: the application reached its daily or monthly verification limit for this channel
errorDetails.destination_country_disabled: destination country is disabled in account settings

smsBlock.note: template is kept when null; autofill is omitted entirely when no marker was stored, and is {"type": "app_hash", "value": "<hash>"} or {"type": "domain", "value": "<the application's SMS domain>"} when one was; the response also carries the deprecated app_hash with the same value for app_hash, which the client does not read. when no template group applies at all, template_group_used is false and template_group and template_fallback_reason are null; group_missing comes with template_group null (the application's group no longer exists)

calloutBlock.note: template_group and template_fallback_reason as for the sms block

autofill.note: sent as sms.autofill: {"type": "app_hash", "value": <appHashFormat>}, {"type": "domain"} or {"type": "none"}; omitted or null takes the application default. A malformed block - not an object, an unknown type, app_hash without a string value, any value with domain or none - is 422 autofill_invalid; a value outside appHashFormat is 422 app_hash_invalid; domain for an application with no SMS domain is 422 sms_domain_not_configured. The deprecated flat sms.app_hash is read only when autofill is absent; a request with both a non-null autofill and a non-null app_hash is 422 autofill_invalid, so the client never sends app_hash

customMaxLength.note: characters; an empty custom is treated as absent, and the value is forwarded to the callback server and never returned

constraints.templateGroup: sent as sms.template_group or callout.template_group to use that template group instead of the application's default; an unknown name is 422 template_group_not_found

codeLength.note: a SERVER fact, now per-application; never compile a length into the client

maxReportAttempts.note: a SERVER fact; the client keeps no attempt counter

constraints.languages: a primary subtag of 2-3 letters and AT MOST ONE more subtag of 2-8 alphanumerics - NARROWER than BCP 47, which is the trap: zh-Hans-CN is well-formed BCP 47 and is REJECTED. Two different failures, do not conflate them: a well-formed tag the channel cannot serve falls back to en-US, while a tag of the wrong SHAPE returns 422 languages_invalid and creates no verification at all. Matched exactly, most preferred first; 'pl' does not match 'pl-PL'. Sent per channel, in the block named after the delivery method - sms.languages and callout.languages take the same tags and only the block matching delivery_method is read, so the other one is ignored rather than rejected
constraints.languageEcho: every channel with a language echoes the tag the SERVER chose as <channel>.language in the response - the first requested tag it could serve, or en-US. It is the only way to detect a fallback, because an unservable tag of the right shape is accepted rather than rejected
constraints.languageSetsDifferPerChannel: the sms and callout tag sets are maintained separately and neither is a subset of the other, so a tag that picks a template on sms may have no recording on callout and fall back silently. Never infer one channel's coverage from the other, and never compile either set into the client - both are SERVER data that changes without a client release
constraints.destinationEcho: stored and echoed DIGITS-ONLY - the leading + is stripped
constraints.destinationValidation: the validator strips only [\s\-()] before matching ^\+?\d{8,15}$, so a dot-formatted number is rejected even though normalisation would have handled it - normalise client-side before sending
constraints.fee: decimal STRING, VAT-inclusive; never parse it
constraints.oneLiveVerificationPerDestination: a start supersedes every unfinished verification for the same application and destination; the superseded row reads status failed with error_code superseded, and is reachable only by id
constraints.deniedStartDoesNotSupersede: a start that is itself DENIED supersedes nothing, so an earlier unfinished verification stays live - and since by_number answers with the newest row whatever its status, that read returns the denied one while the live verification is reachable only by the id its own start returned
constraints.byNumberResolution: the newest verification for that destination, whatever its status - NOT 'the live one'

finishedRetention.note: a finished verification is hard-deleted after this, so a later read by id or by number answers 404 rather than the outcome; persist anything needed beyond the window

constraints.reportBeforeDispatch: 'pending' spans a window in which a report is refused with not_ready_to_report (422): the status is already public and the row underneath it has not finished dispatching, so the code is retryable rather than terminal
constraints.tooManyRequests: 429 carries one of: destination_in_cooldown (a verification for this destination was requested too recently), rate_limit_per_ip (too many requests from this IP address), rate_limit_failed_auth (too many failed authentication attempts from this IP address), rate_limit_per_account (too many requests for this account), rate_limit_public_per_account (too many public requests for this account) or volume_limit_reached (the application reached its daily or monthly verification limit for this delivery method). Wait the number of seconds in Retry-After before trying again; for volume_limit_reached it can be long (days), so surface it instead of retrying
